US.description: Higher than average, reflecting costs for groceries, transportation, healthcare, and utilities across various regions.

IN.description: Covers essential groceries, local transportation, utilities, and a modest budget for dining and entertainment for a single person.

SG.description: High costs for transport, groceries, and dining out, but public services are efficient.

CH.description: Very high costs for groceries, public transport, personal services, and dining out. Healthcare is also expensive.

NL.description: Reflects higher costs for groceries, public transportation, and leisure activities compared to the baseline.

GB.description: Covers groceries, public transport, utilities, and typical leisure activities for a single person, excluding rent.

CA.description: Covers groceries, local transportation, utilities, basic entertainment, and personal care items.

AE.description: High cost of living, with significant expenses for dining out, entertainment, and utilities, while groceries and transport (with own car) can be moderate.

NO.description: High costs for groceries, transportation, and dining out are typical across Norway.

IE.description: High costs across categories like groceries, utilities, and transport; dining out is particularly expensive.

LU.description: Cost of living is high, particularly for groceries, dining, and personal services. Public transport is free, which helps offset some costs.

AU.description: Reflects typical monthly expenses for groceries, transport, utilities, and leisure in Australian cities, excluding rent.

QA.description: Reflects costs for groceries, transportation, utilities, and leisure activities in Doha.

BN.description: Cost of living excluding rent is moderate to low, with affordable groceries, utilities, and local transportation. Dining out at local restaurants is inexpensive.

MO.description: High cost for groceries, dining, and transportation, reflecting its status as a major tourist and business hub.
